files.content:
name: API Contract Tests

# This workflow tests your API against the OpenAPI spec using Schemathesis.
# It only runs the "examples" phase (fast & deterministic).
# For thorough fuzzing, run locally: make schemathesis

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**.go'
      - 'go.mod'
      - 'go.sum'
      - 'openapi.yaml'
      - 'cmd/**'
      - 'internal/**'
      - 'pkg/**'
      - '.github/workflows/api-contract-tests.yml'

concurrency:
  group: api-contract-tests-${{ github.head_ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  api-contract-tests:
    name: API Contract Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10

    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg18
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: test_db
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/test_db?sslmode=disable
      API_KEY: [REDACTED]
      PORT: 8080

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: '1.27.2'

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/go-build
            ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-go-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod download

      - name: Install goose
        run: go install github.com/pressly/goose/v3/cmd/goose@v3.28.0

      - name: Validate migrations
        run: make migrate-validate

      - name: Initialize database schema
        run: make init-db

      - name: Run River migrations
        run: |
          go install github.com/riverqueue/river/cmd/river@v0.49.0
          make river-migrate

      - name: Build application
        run: make build

      - name: Start API server
        run: |
          ./bin/hub-api &
          API_PID=$!
          echo "API_PID=$API_PID" >> $GITHUB_ENV

          # Wait for server to be healthy (up to ~60s)
          for i in {1..30}; do
            if curl -s http://localhost:8080/health | grep -q "OK"; then
              echo "Server is ready"
              break
            fi
            echo "Waiting for server... ($i/30)"
            sleep 2
          done

          # Verify we actually became ready
          if ! curl -s http://localhost:8080/health | grep -q "OK"; then
            echo "Server failed to start. Checking logs..."
            ps aux | grep api || true
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.14'

      - name: Install Schemathesis
        run: python -m pip install schemathesis==4.30.0

      # Endpoints that depend on optional Hub features (embeddings, the taxonomy
      # compute service) legitimately return a documented 503 when those features
      # are not configured — and they are not configured in this CI job. They are
      # excluded from this run (which enforces not_a_server_error) and validated in
      # the next step with that check dropped, so their documented 503 still passes
      # status/content/schema conformance without being flagged as a server error.
      - name: Run API contract tests
        env:
          SCHEMATHESIS_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8080
          SCHEMATHESIS_WAIT_FOR_SCHEMA: '2'
        run: |
          schemathesis run ./openapi.yaml \
            --generation-database=:memory: \
            --max-examples=100 \
            --checks=not_a_server_error,status_code_conformance,content_type_conformance,response_schema_conformance \
            --phases examples \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer test-api-key-for-ci" \
            --exclude-operation-id semantic-search-feedback-records \
            --exclude-operation-id similar-feedback-records \
            --exclude-operation-id list-taxonomy-fields \
            --exclude-operation-id create-taxonomy-run

      # Embedding/taxonomy-service-dependent endpoints: not_a_server_error is dropped
      # because a 503 (feature not configured in CI) is expected and documented; the
      # remaining checks still enforce the response conforms to the spec.
      - name: Run API contract tests (embedding-dependent endpoints)
        env:
          SCHEMATHESIS_BASE_URL: http://localhost:8080
          SCHEMATHESIS_WAIT_FOR_SCHEMA: '2'
        run: |
          schemathesis run ./openapi.yaml \
            --generation-database=:memory: \
            --max-examples=100 \
            --checks=status_code_conformance,content_type_conformance,response_schema_conformance \
            --phases examples \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer test-api-key-for-ci" \
            --include-operation-id semantic-search-feedback-records \
            --include-operation-id similar-feedback-records \
            --include-operation-id list-taxonomy-fields \
            --include-operation-id create-taxonomy-run

      - name: Stop API server
        if: always()
        run: |
          if [ ! -z "$API_PID" ]; then
            kill $API_PID || true
          fi
          pkill -f "./bin/hub-api" || true

name: SDK preview

# Shows what a spec change does to the published SDK surface. The generated SDK is
# not committed, so a PR touching openapi.yaml otherwise says nothing about its
# effect on @formbricks/hub — this is the replacement for the preview the previous
# generator's action used to comment on every PR.
#
# SECURITY: this job runs the generator over PR-controlled files (openapi.yaml, and
# the generator config and lockfile when sdks/** is touched), so it is treated as
# executing untrusted code:
#   - `pull_request`, never `pull_request_target` (which would hand fork content a
#     writable token and the base repo's secrets — GitHub's "pwn request").
#   - read-only permissions, no secrets, no environment.
#   - --ignore-scripts on install.
#   - output goes to the job summary rather than a PR comment, so no write token is
#     needed anywhere. If a comment is ever wanted, the safe shape is an artifact
#     plus a separate workflow_run job that never checks out the PR ref.

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'openapi.yaml'
      - 'sdks/**'
      - '.github/workflows/sdk-preview.yml'

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # Must match NPM_VERSION in publish-sdk.yml, so every SDK pull request runs the
  # packing and comparison under the npm a release will use — npm's JSON output
  # changes between majors, and this is where that should surface, not on the
  # first release after a bump.
  NPM_VERSION: 12.2.0

concurrency:
  group: sdk-preview-${{ github.head_ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Diff the SDK surface
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: sdks/typescript

    steps:
      # persist-credentials: false — this job runs PR-controlled code through the
      # generator, so leaving the checkout token in .git/config would put it
      # within reach of that code. Nothing here does an authenticated git
      # operation after checkout.
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0
        with:
          package_json_file: sdks/typescript/package.json

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: pnpm
          cache-dependency-path: sdks/typescript/pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

      - name: Pin npm
        run: npm install -g --ignore-scripts "npm@${NPM_VERSION}"

      - name: Generate and build
        run: pnpm build

      - name: Type check
        run: ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit

      # Wire tests for the generated client, plus the comparison and publish-guard
      # scripts the release workflow depends on.
      - name: Tests
        run: node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs'

      # Compares the public surface against what is on npm today: the export map
      # subpath by subpath, and the exported names of each entry point read from
      # the built declarations and runtime files. A rename or a removal here is a
      # breaking change for consumers and should be visible in review, not
      # discovered after the release.
      #
      # Both sides are packed the way npm packs them, so `files` applies to the
      # generated side too and what is compared is what would actually ship. The
      # packing, fetching and npm error handling are shared with publish-sdk.yml
      # via scripts/prepare-comparison.mjs, so the preview a reviewer reads and
      # the release's summary measure the same two packages the same way.
      - name: Diff the public surface against the package on npm
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PREP="$(node scripts/prepare-comparison.mjs .compare)"
          echo "$PREP"

          ON_NPM="$(PREP="$PREP" node -p 'JSON.parse(process.env.PREP).publishedVersion ?? ""')"
          if [ -z "$ON_NPM" ]; then
            echo "\`@formbricks/hub\` is not on npm yet; nothing to compare." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi

          node scripts/surface.mjs .compare/published .compare/generated "$ON_NPM" \
            >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Publish TypeScript SDK

# Generates @formbricks/hub from openapi.yaml and publishes it to npm on every
# stable Hub release, under the release's own version: @formbricks/hub@X is the
# client for Hub X. The SDK is a build artifact — nothing generated is committed,
# and its version is stamped from the tag — so this workflow is the only place
# it is produced.
#
# SECURITY: this file's name is part of npm's trusted-publisher binding
# (formbricks/hub + publish-sdk.yml + the npm-publish environment). Do not rename
# it without updating the npm configuration, and do not add a pull_request-family
# trigger here: PR-time generation lives in sdk-preview.yml, which holds no
# credentials. Only a release tag publishes — a manual run can dry-run from any
# ref, but publishes only from a tag. See AGENTS.md -> TypeScript SDK.

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry_run:
        description: "Build and compare, but do not publish"
        type: boolean
        default: true

# Least privilege by default; the publish job opts into id-token explicitly.
permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  # The npm both jobs use, defined once on purpose: the publish job re-packs the
  # artifact and requires the build job's integrity hash, and two npm versions
  # can pack one tree differently, so the two must not drift apart. sdk-preview.yml
  # pins the same version, so every SDK pull request exercises the npm a release
  # will use. npm 12 needs Node ^24.15.0; setup-node's '24' resolves above that.
  NPM_VERSION: 12.2.0

concurrency:
  # One package-wide group, not per-release: the compare step plans the
  # dist-tag from every version already on npm, so two concurrent releases
  # could plan against the same list and race. A second release queues behind
  # the running one; GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so a third
  # release cancels the second's pending run, which then has to be re-run.
  group: publish-sdk
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Runs third-party code (the generator, its dependencies, the build) and so
  # deliberately holds NO publishing credential. Everything it produces is handed
  # to the publish job as an artifact.
  build:
    name: Generate, test and pack
    # Prereleases are skipped, matching hub-release.yml's Docker builds. Gated on
    # the job so the run is genuinely skipped — a step that exited non-zero would
    # mark every prerelease as a failed workflow.
    if: github.event_name != 'release' || github.event.release.prerelease == false
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: sdks/typescript
    outputs:
      should_publish: ${{ steps.compare.outputs.should_publish }}
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      # `latest`, or `release-X.Y` for a backport; see the compare step.
      dist_tag: ${{ steps.compare.outputs.dist_tag }}
      # The identity of the tarball this job packed and compared. The publish job
      # re-packs the artifact and refuses to publish anything else.
      pack_integrity: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.integrity }}

    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@ccd8616d44fd3846e67624a50d5aad6d37bf2d25 # v2.22.1
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      # persist-credentials: false — this job runs the generator and its
      # dependencies, so leaving the checkout token in .git/config would put it
      # within reach of that code. Nothing here does an authenticated git
      # operation after checkout, and the publish job holds no checkout at all.
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up pnpm
        uses: pnpm/action-setup@ea17c68df8912ef543352723c149a84f56e3d413 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # Relative to the repo root, not to defaults.run.working-directory.
          package_json_file: sdks/typescript/package.json

      # No dependency cache in a release build. What this job produces is what
      # gets published, and its integrity hash is computed here too, so a poisoned
      # cache would poison the package with nothing downstream able to tell —
      # setup-node's own guidance is to disable caching in publishing workflows.
      # It costs one uncached install per release; the lockfile's integrity
      # hashes still verify every download.
      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false

      # --ignore-scripts: nothing here needs a native build step, and lifecycle
      # scripts are the entry point for install-time supply-chain attacks.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

      # The SDK's version is the Hub release's, stamped into package.json from the
      # tag before anything is built or packed, so nobody bumps it by hand. A tag
      # that is not a plain X.Y.Z fails here. Off a tag — a dry run from a branch
      # — the committed placeholder version is kept. GITHUB_REF_TYPE and
      # GITHUB_REF_NAME come from the runner. See scripts/release-version.mjs.
      - name: Take the version from the release tag
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          VERSION="$(node scripts/release-version.mjs stamp)"
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Target version: $VERSION"

      - name: Generate and build
        run: pnpm build

      - name: Type check
        run: ./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit

      # The wire tests pin the regression that motivated leaving the previous
      # generator (array filters must go out as repeated query parameters); the
      # rest cover the comparison and publish-guard scripts this workflow runs.
      - name: Tests
        run: node --test 'tests/*.test.mjs'

      # Same npm as the publish job — see NPM_VERSION at the top.
      - name: Pin npm
        run: npm install -g --ignore-scripts "npm@${NPM_VERSION}"

      # Packs this package and fetches the one on npm. Shared with sdk-preview.yml
      # so the release's summary and the preview a reviewer reads are measured
      # the same way. See scripts/prepare-comparison.mjs for the npm behaviour it
      # absorbs — notably that `npm view` failing does not mean "not published".
      - name: Pack and fetch the package on npm
        id: pack
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          PREP="$(node scripts/prepare-comparison.mjs .compare)"
          echo "$PREP"
          {
            echo "integrity=$(PREP="$PREP" node -p 'JSON.parse(process.env.PREP).integrity')"
            echo "on_npm=$(PREP="$PREP" node -p 'JSON.parse(process.env.PREP).publishedVersion ?? ""')"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Every stable Hub release publishes its SDK, so each Hub version has a
      # client with the same version — including a release whose SDK is otherwise
      # unchanged since the last one. The comparison against the package on npm
      # stays, for the job summary: it shows what the release changes for SDK
      # users. It covers everything the package ships — build output, sources,
      # manifest and documentation — minus the version, which is the input.
      #
      # It also decides the npm dist-tag, from every version already published
      # (scripts/release-version.mjs `plan`): `latest` for a release above all of
      # them, `release-X.Y` for a backport — a 0.14.1 security fix released after
      # 0.15.0, which Hub releases as stable but not latest — so `latest` never
      # moves backwards. What stops a release here, before the publish job
      # starts: a version npm already has, and a backport older than one
      # already published on its line.
      - name: Compare against the package on npm
        id: compare
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
          ON_NPM: ${{ steps.pack.outputs.on_npm }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.dry_run }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if [ -z "$ON_NPM" ]; then
            echo "::notice::@formbricks/hub is not on npm yet — publishing $VERSION."
          else
            echo "On npm: $ON_NPM / building: $VERSION"

            STATUS=0
            node scripts/compare-packed.mjs .compare/published .compare/generated \
              > .compare/packed-diff.txt || STATUS=$?

            if [ "$STATUS" -eq 2 ]; then
              echo "::error::compare-packed.mjs could not compare the two packages — see the log above."
              exit 1
            fi

            if [ "$STATUS" -eq 0 ]; then
              echo "::notice::Packed contents are unchanged since @formbricks/hub@$ON_NPM; publishing $VERSION anyway, so this Hub release has its SDK."
            else
              PATHS="$(wc -l < .compare/packed-diff.txt | tr -d ' ')"
              echo "Packed contents differ from @formbricks/hub@$ON_NPM ($PATHS paths):"
              {
                echo '```'
                head -100 .compare/packed-diff.txt
                echo '```'
              } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            fi
          fi

          # Only a release publishes, so only a tag is planned; a dry run from a
          # branch builds the committed placeholder version.
          if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" = "tag" ]; then
            # A package with nothing published is a 404, so an empty list; any
            # other failure to read the registry stops the release.
            if ! npm view @formbricks/hub versions --json \
              > .compare/versions.json 2> .compare/versions.err; then
              if grep -q E404 .compare/versions.err; then
                echo "[]" > .compare/versions.json
              else
                cat .compare/versions.err
                echo "::error::Could not read @formbricks/hub's published versions from npm."
                exit 1
              fi
            fi

            REFUSED=0
            DIST_TAG="$(node scripts/release-version.mjs plan "$VERSION" .compare/versions.json)" || REFUSED=1
            if [ "$REFUSED" -ne 0 ]; then
              if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
                echo "::warning::A release from this tag would not publish — see above."
                echo "should_publish=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "::error::Not publishing @formbricks/hub@$VERSION — see above."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "Publishing $VERSION under the $DIST_TAG dist-tag."
            echo "dist_tag=$DIST_TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

          echo "should_publish=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Hands over the publishable directory rather than the .tgz: `npm publish`
      # from a package directory is the documented provenance path, and npm's docs
      # do not commit either way on whether provenance is generated when
      # publishing a pre-packed tarball. Not the place to find out.
      - name: Upload the publishable package
        if: steps.compare.outputs.should_publish == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: npm-package
          path: |
            sdks/typescript/dist
            sdks/typescript/src
            sdks/typescript/package.json
            sdks/typescript/README.md
            sdks/typescript/LICENSE
          retention-days: 7
          if-no-files-found: error

  # Checks, before the publish job can so much as request the npm-publish
  # environment, that this is a release tag, that its commit is on the default
  # branch, and that the environment exists and is protected. The last is the
  # one that matters most: a job that references a missing environment creates
  # it with no protection rules and carries on, so without this the first
  # release would publish through an unprotected environment and look like a
  # success. See scripts/verify-publish-guards.mjs for the checks themselves,
  # and for what they deliberately cannot do.
  #
  # Its own job, so the checks run with first-party code only: the build job
  # runs the generator's dependencies and should not hold `actions: read`, and
  # the publish job must not start at all if a check fails. It runs alongside
  # the build rather than after it, so a misconfigured release path surfaces
  # while the build runs, before the publish job can start.
  #
  # A dry run from a tag runs it too, which makes that a full rehearsal of the
  # release path — environment and token permissions included — that publishes
  # nothing. A dry run from a branch skips it, since the ref check would fail
  # for a run that was never going to publish.
  guards:
    name: Verify publish guards
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'release' && github.event.release.prerelease == false) ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
        (!inputs.dry_run || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')))
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read # the compare API: is the tagged commit on the default branch?
      actions: read # the environments API

    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@ccd8616d44fd3846e67624a50d5aad6d37bf2d25 # v2.22.1
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      # persist-credentials: false — nothing here does a git operation, and the
      # token the check needs is passed to it explicitly below.
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false

      # GITHUB_REF, GITHUB_SHA and GITHUB_REPOSITORY come from the runner, so
      # nothing ref-derived is interpolated into this script.
      - name: Verify the publish guards
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # Must match the publish job's `environment:` and the environment named
          # in npm's trusted-publisher configuration.
          PUBLISH_ENVIRONMENT: npm-publish
        run: node sdks/typescript/scripts/verify-publish-guards.mjs

  # Holds the publish credential and nothing else: it downloads the packed
  # package and runs npm publish with lifecycle scripts disabled, so none of the
  # code the build job produced runs alongside the credential. No checkout, no
  # install, no repo or dependency code — a compromised dev dependency in the
  # build job cannot reach npm.
  publish:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: [build, guards]
    # Tags only, matching the guards job's own check: a release is a tag, and a
    # manual run from a branch must not reach the environment at all. `needs`
    # also means a failed or skipped guards job skips this one.
    if: >-
      needs.build.outputs.should_publish == 'true' &&
      startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') &&
      !(github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.dry_run)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Gates the OIDC token behind the environment's protection rules. npm's
    # trusted-publisher binding covers this repository, this workflow file and
    # this environment's name, but not the ref, so the environment's rules are
    # what decide which runs can publish. The guards job has already confirmed
    # they exist; AGENTS.md has the configuration they should have.
    environment: npm-publish
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - name: Harden the runner
        uses: step-security/harden-runner@ccd8616d44fd3846e67624a50d5aad6d37bf2d25 # v2.22.1
        with:
          egress-policy: audit

      - name: Download the publishable package
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: npm-package
          path: package

      # Trusted publishing needs npm >= 11.5.1, and the runner's bundled npm is
      # whatever the Node image shipped with, so the npm is pinned below. Node
      # first: both the validation and that install need it. No cache, per
      # setup-node's guidance for publishing workflows: in this job a poisoned
      # cache would sit next to the OIDC token.
      #
      # No registry-url, deliberately: setup-node would write an .npmrc whose
      # _authToken is ${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}. With no token set, npm presents that
      # placeholder when the OIDC exchange fails, and the registry answers the
      # PUT with a 404 — the misleading error Hub 0.9.0's publish got. Without
      # it, a failed exchange is an honest ENEEDAUTH; the publish names the
      # registry with --registry.
      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false

      # Before the checks below, because the integrity one has to run under the
      # same npm the build job packed with. --ignore-scripts: nothing here needs
      # an install hook either.
      - name: Pin an OIDC-capable npm
        run: npm install -g --ignore-scripts "npm@${NPM_VERSION}"

      # The artifact is produced by the build job, which runs third-party code,
      # so it is treated as untrusted input here: `npm publish` would otherwise
      # execute whatever lifecycle hooks its manifest defines, in this job, with
      # the OIDC token in scope. --ignore-scripts on the publish command is the
      # enforcement; this step is what makes the difference visible, and what
      # pins the identity of the package being sent to the registry.
      - name: Validate the package before it is sent to the registry
        working-directory: package
        env:
          EXPECTED_NAME: '@formbricks/hub'
          EXPECTED_VERSION: '${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}'
          EXPECTED_DIST_TAG: '${{ needs.build.outputs.dist_tag }}'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node --input-type=commonjs - <<'NODE'
          const { readFileSync } = require("node:fs");

          const manifest = JSON.parse(readFileSync("package.json", "utf8"));

          function assert(condition, message) {
            if (condition) return;
            console.error(`::error::${message}`);
            process.exit(1);
          }

          assert(
            manifest.name === process.env.EXPECTED_NAME,
            `The package is named ${manifest.name}, expected ${process.env.EXPECTED_NAME}.`,
          );
          assert(
            manifest.version === process.env.EXPECTED_VERSION,
            `The package is at version ${manifest.version} but the build job reported ${process.env.EXPECTED_VERSION}.`,
          );

          // The version is the release tag's, so it is checked against the tag
          // itself — GITHUB_REF_NAME, set by the runner in this job — and not
          // only against what the build job reported. That job runs third-party
          // code, which could rewrite both the manifest and its own outputs; this
          // way, whoever creates the release of tag X knows X is what publishes.
          // The pattern must stay the one in scripts/release-version.mjs, which
          // this job cannot load (it has no checkout); a test pins the two equal.
          const RELEASE = /^v?(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)\.(0|[1-9]\d*)$/;
          assert(
            process.env.GITHUB_REF_TYPE === "tag",
            `This run is for a ${process.env.GITHUB_REF_TYPE}, not a release tag.`,
          );
          const tag = RELEASE.exec(process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME ?? "");
          assert(
            tag !== null,
            `The release tag ${JSON.stringify(process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME)} is not a plain X.Y.Z version.`,
          );
          const tagVersion = `${tag[1]}.${tag[2]}.${tag[3]}`;
          assert(
            manifest.version === tagVersion,
            `The package is at version ${manifest.version} but the release tag is ${tagVersion}.`,
          );

          // The dist-tag comes from the build job too, so it is held to the only
          // two the tag allows: `latest` — published with no --tag, so npm
          // itself refuses it for anything below the highest version — or this
          // version's own backport line. Nothing else can be named.
          const lineTag = `release-${tag[1]}.${tag[2]}`;
          assert(
            process.env.EXPECTED_DIST_TAG === "latest" ||
              process.env.EXPECTED_DIST_TAG === lineTag,
            `The build job chose the dist-tag ${JSON.stringify(process.env.EXPECTED_DIST_TAG)}, but tag ${tagVersion} can only publish under "latest" or "${lineTag}".`,
          );

          // npm runs these out of the manifest while packing and while publishing.
          // --ignore-scripts skips them; rejecting them here means a manifest that
          // tries is reported rather than silently ignored.
          const HOOKS = [
            "prepublish",
            "prepare",
            "prepublishOnly",
            "prepack",
            "postpack",
            "publish",
            "postpublish",
          ];
          const hooks = Object.keys(manifest.scripts ?? {}).filter((name) =>
            HOOKS.includes(name),
          );
          assert(
            hooks.length === 0,
            `The package defines lifecycle scripts that would run during a publish: ${hooks.join(", ")}.`,
          );

          // npm reads publishConfig during a publish, and it is where a manifest
          // could redirect the registry, retag the release or switch provenance
          // off. Allowing only the one key this package legitimately sets closes
          // the whole field, rather than the handful of keys that came to mind:
          // registry, tag, access and provenance all come from the command line.
          const ALLOWED_PUBLISH_CONFIG = ["access"];
          const unexpected = Object.keys(manifest.publishConfig ?? {}).filter(
            (key) => !ALLOWED_PUBLISH_CONFIG.includes(key),
          );
          assert(
            unexpected.length === 0,
            `The package sets publishConfig keys that could steer the publish: ${unexpected.join(", ")}. Only ${ALLOWED_PUBLISH_CONFIG.join(", ")} is expected here.`,
          );

          console.log(
            `Validated ${manifest.name}@${manifest.version}: the release tag's version, no publish lifecycle scripts, no publishConfig override.`,
          );
          NODE

      # The build job compared a packed tarball against npm to decide that this
      # release should publish, and tested the tree it came from. This re-packs
      # the downloaded artifact and requires the same integrity hash, so what
      # reaches the registry is the package that was compared and tested — not
      # merely something with a plausible manifest. It closes the gap between the
      # two jobs: a tampered or truncated artifact fails here rather than
      # shipping. `npm pack` is reproducible for a given tree and npm version,
      # which is why both jobs pin the same npm.
      #
      # This is an integrity check, not a trust check: the build job produces both
      # the artifact and the expected hash, so a compromise *inside* that job
      # would match. Keeping code out of this job is what the validation above and
      # --ignore-scripts below are for.
      - name: Verify the artifact is the package the build job compared
        working-directory: package
        env:
          EXPECTED_INTEGRITY: ${{ needs.build.outputs.pack_integrity }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$EXPECTED_INTEGRITY" ]; then
            echo "::error::The build job recorded no packed integrity; refusing to publish unverified contents."
            exit 1
          fi
          # npm 11 prints `npm pack --json` as an array of entries; npm 12 as an
          # object keyed by package name. Read either, so an npm bump cannot turn
          # into a gate that compares against `undefined` and blocks every release.
          ACTUAL="$(npm pack --ignore-scripts --dry-run --json | node -e '
            const json = JSON.parse(require("node:fs").readFileSync(0, "utf8"));
            const entry = Array.isArray(json)
              ? json[0]
              : json?.filename ? json : Object.values(json ?? {})[0];
            if (typeof entry?.integrity !== "string") process.exit(1);
            console.log(entry.integrity);
          ')"
          echo "expected: $EXPECTED_INTEGRITY"
          echo "actual:   $ACTUAL"
          if [ "$ACTUAL" != "$EXPECTED_INTEGRITY" ]; then
            echo "::error::The downloaded package does not match what the build job packed and compared. Not publishing."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Artifact matches the tarball the build job compared."

      # No NPM_TOKEN anywhere: authentication is OIDC via the trusted publisher.
      # A missing credential must fail, never fall back to a token.
      #
      # --ignore-scripts: the manifest was checked in the step above, and this is
      # what keeps pack and publish lifecycle hooks from the artifact out of this
      # credential-bearing job.
      #
      # --registry: named explicitly so the target of the publish, and therefore
      # who the OIDC token is presented to, does not come from the artifact.
      #
      # --provenance is passed explicitly even though trusted publishing is
      # documented as generating attestations automatically: the two npm docs
      # pages disagree on whether the flag is needed, and passing it when it is
      # already implied is harmless while omitting it when it is not is silent.
      #
      # No --tag for a latest release, deliberately. The dist-tag defaults to
      # `latest` anyway, and leaving it implicit keeps npm's own guard: it refuses
      # to apply `latest` implicitly to a prerelease, or to a version lower than
      # the highest published. Passing `--tag latest` explicitly switches that
      # guard off, and would let a hand-edited version move `latest` backwards
      # for everyone. A backport passes `--tag release-X.Y`, which never names
      # `latest`, so it cannot move it either.
      #
      # On failure it prints npm's own trusted-publishing lines. npm reports a
      # refused OIDC exchange only as a missing login, and records why at verbose
      # level, which its debug log always keeps whatever the console level. A
      # successful exchange is logged there too, so a publish refused after one
      # — a trusted publisher limited to `npm stage publish`, say — reads
      # differently from one never authorised. Only the `oidc` lines are shown;
      # npm never logs a token.
      - name: Publish
        working-directory: package
        env:
          DIST_TAG: ${{ needs.build.outputs.dist_tag }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Publishing $(node -p "require('./package.json').name")@$(node -p "require('./package.json').version") under $DIST_TAG"
          TAG_ARGS=()
          if [ "$DIST_TAG" != "latest" ]; then
            TAG_ARGS=(--tag "$DIST_TAG")
          fi
          # Its own logs directory, so the debug log read below is this
          # publish's and no earlier npm command's.
          LOGS="$RUNNER_TEMP/npm-publish-logs"
          if ! npm publish \
            --access public \
            --provenance \
            --ignore-scripts \
            --registry https://registry.npmjs.org/ \
            --logs-dir "$LOGS" \
            "${TAG_ARGS[@]}"; then
            echo "::group::npm's trusted-publishing (OIDC) log"
            grep -hE '^[0-9]+ (verbose|silly) oidc ' "$LOGS"/*-debug-*.log ||
              echo "(no OIDC lines: npm did not attempt the token exchange, or wrote no log)"
            echo "::endgroup::"
            exit 1
          fi

      # `npm view` exits 0 and prints nothing when the field is absent, so a bare
      # `if npm view …; then` succeeds on the first pass with no attestation at
      # all. The output is captured and parsed instead, and the step fails if no
      # verifiable attestation shows up: provenance is the reason the package is
      # published by this workflow rather than from a laptop.
      - name: Confirm the provenance attestation landed
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          for i in $(seq 1 10); do
            # stderr is kept: a registry that cannot be read and an attestation that
            # was never created look identical from here, and the failure below is
            # easier to read with npm's own error above it.
            ATTESTATIONS="$(npm view "@formbricks/hub@$VERSION" dist.attestations --json 2>npm-view.err || true)"
            if ATTESTATIONS="$ATTESTATIONS" node -e '
              let attestations;
              try {
                attestations = JSON.parse(process.env.ATTESTATIONS);
              } catch {
                process.exit(1);
              }
              // npm 12 wraps every `npm view --json` result in an array.
              if (Array.isArray(attestations)) attestations = attestations[0];
              const url = attestations?.url;
              const predicateType = attestations?.provenance?.predicateType;
              process.exit(
                typeof url === "string" &&
                  url.startsWith("https://registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/attestations/") &&
                  predicateType === "https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1"
                  ? 0
                  : 1,
              );
            '; then
              echo "Provenance attestation present for $VERSION: $ATTESTATIONS"
              exit 0
            fi
            sleep 10
          done
          tail -3 npm-view.err 2>/dev/null || true
          echo "::error::No verifiable provenance attestation for @formbricks/hub@$VERSION after 100s. Check npmjs.com, and do not describe this release as provenance-signed until it is there."
          exit 1

name: Tests

# This workflow runs unit and integration tests

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**.go'
      - 'go.mod'
      - 'go.sum'
      - 'Makefile'
      - 'migrations/**'
      - 'tests/**'
      - '.githooks/**'
      - '.github/workflows/tests.yml'

concurrency:
  group: tests-${{ github.head_ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  unit-tests:
    name: Unit Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: '1.27.2'

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/go-build
            ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-go-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod download

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: make test-unit

  integration-tests:
    name: Integration Tests (${{ matrix.postgres_image }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        postgres_image: [pg16, pg17, pg18]

    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:${{ matrix.postgres_image }}
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: test_db
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/test_db?sslmode=disable
      API_KEY: [REDACTED]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: '1.27.2'

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/go-build
            ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-go-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod download

      - name: Install goose
        run: go install github.com/pressly/goose/v3/cmd/goose@v3.28.0

      - name: Validate migrations
        run: make migrate-validate

      - name: Initialize database schema
        run: make init-db

      - name: Run River migrations
        run: |
          go install github.com/riverqueue/river/cmd/river@v0.49.0
          make river-migrate

      - name: Run integration tests
        run: make tests

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10

    services:
      postgres:
        image: pgvector/pgvector:pg18
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: test_db
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/test_db?sslmode=disable
      API_KEY: [REDACTED]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@b7ad1dad31e06c5925ef5d2fc7ad053ef454303e # v7.0.0
        with:
          go-version: '1.27.2'

      - name: Cache Go modules
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/go-build
            ~/go/pkg/mod
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-go-${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-go-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: go mod download

      - name: Install goose
        run: go install github.com/pressly/goose/v3/cmd/goose@v3.28.0

      - name: Initialize database schema
        run: make init-db

      - name: Run River migrations
        run: |
          go install github.com/riverqueue/river/cmd/river@v0.49.0
          make river-migrate

      - name: Check coverage (excludes cmd/api)
        run: make check-coverage

  tests:
    name: All Tests
    needs: [unit-tests, integration-tests, coverage]
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Check test results
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.unit-tests.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Unit tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.integration-tests.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Integration tests failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "${{ needs.coverage.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "Coverage check failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "✅ All tests passed!"

# @formbricks/hub

The official TypeScript client for the [Formbricks Hub](https://hub.formbricks.com) API — feedback-record storage, search, enrichment and webhooks.

```bash
npm install @formbricks/hub
```

On Node.js, 22 or later. The client is built on the standard `fetch`, so it also runs in browsers and Bun. Deno is not supported yet: the generated client passes its `client` option through to `new Request()`, which Deno rejects.

## Usage

```ts
import { createHubClient, listFeedbackRecords } from "@formbricks/hub";

const client = createHubClient({
  apiKey: [REDACTED],
  baseUrl: "https://app.formbricks.com", // or your self-hosted Hub
});

const { data } = await listFeedbackRecords({
  client,
  query: {
    tenant_id: "org-123",
    source_type: ["survey", "review"],
    sentiment: ["negative", "very_negative"],
    limit: 50,
  },
});
```

`baseUrl` is required rather than defaulted: the Hub is self-hostable, so there is no single correct origin.

Every operation is a standalone function, so bundlers can tree-shake what you don't call. If you need interceptors or extra headers, use the generated client directly — and pass it `createHubFetch()` to keep the retries described below:

```ts
import { createClient, createConfig, createHubFetch } from "@formbricks/hub";

const client = createClient(
  createConfig({ baseUrl, auth: () => apiKey, fetch: createHubFetch() }),
);
```

Calls return `{ data, error, response }` rather than throwing on an error status; pass `throwOnError: true` to throw the parsed error body instead. Network failures and timeouts come back in `error` the same way.

## Retries and timeouts

Requests are retried and timed out by default: up to **2 retries**, **60 seconds per attempt**, exponential backoff with jitter, and a server's `Retry-After` honoured. A request is only sent again when that cannot apply it twice — with one exception, below the table:

| Retried                                        | On                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Any request                                    | `429`; a `408` or `503` with `Retry-After`; a `409` whose problem `code` is `tenant_write_conflict` |
| `GET`, `HEAD`, `OPTIONS`, `PUT`, `DELETE` also | `500`, `502`, `504`, any other `408` or `503`, network errors, timed-out attempts                   |

`POST` and `PATCH` are not retried after a `500`, `502` or `504`, a `408` or `503` without `Retry-After`, a network error or a timeout, because the Hub may already have applied them. A proxy such as Envoy or Istio answers `503` when its connection to the Hub drops and `408` when its idle timeout fires, either of which can follow a committed write. A create the Hub already applied would come back as a `409` conflict, or — for a webhook — be created twice. Retry those deliberately if your call is safe to repeat, such as a semantic search. Other `4xx` responses are never retried, nor is a request you abort, nor a response whose `Retry-After` asks for more than 60 seconds: that response is returned for you to act on.

A `DELETE` retried after its response was lost can answer `404`: the first attempt already deleted it. The exception is the tenant purge, `DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/feedback-records`: a purge requested after an earlier one finished starts a new run, so if the first purge's response is lost and that purge completes before the retry, the retry also deletes feedback ingested in between. If that matters, call it with `maxRetries: 0` and check its progress instead.

If you run the Hub behind your own proxy, don't have it turn upstream errors into `503` with `Retry-After` — that marks a request the Hub never saw, so `POST`s would be re-sent.

```ts
const client = createHubClient({
  apiKey,
  baseUrl,
  maxRetries: 4, // 0 turns retries off
  timeout: 10_000, // per attempt, in ms; 0 turns it off
});
```

The timeout covers each attempt until its body has been read, so a response that stalls mid-body can't hang a call; set `timeout: 0` for a long-lived stream. For `GET`, `OPTIONS`, `PUT` and `DELETE`, while a retry is still possible, a JSON body is read inside the attempt, so one that drops or stalls mid-response is retried like any other failure. A retried response's body is discarded unread, except a `409`'s, of which up to 64 KB is read for its `code`. The timeout applies to each attempt separately; to bound a call as a whole, pass a `signal`, e.g. `AbortSignal.timeout(30_000)`.

Retries live in the client's `fetch`. A `fetch` passed per call, or set later with `client.setConfig({ fetch })`, replaces them unless it is a `createHubFetch()` itself.

## Runtime validation

Zod schemas for every request and response shape — carrying the spec's own `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern` and enum constraints — are available from a separate entry point, so importing the client itself pulls in no dependencies:

```ts
import { zFeedbackRecordData } from "@formbricks/hub/schemas";
```

`zod` is an optional peer dependency; install it only if you use this entry point.

## Repeated query parameters

Array filters are sent as repeated parameters (`?source_type=survey&source_type=review`), which is what the Hub expects — it does not split comma-separated values. Pass arrays and the client does the right thing.

## How this package is built

It is generated from [`openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/formbricks/hub/blob/main/openapi.yaml) in the Hub repository by [`@hey-api/openapi-ts`](https://heyapi.dev/), and published from that repository on every stable Hub release with [npm provenance](https://docs.npmjs.com/generating-provenance-statements). Its version is the Hub release's: `@formbricks/hub@0.14.0` is the client for Hub 0.14.0, so pin the SDK to the Hub version you run. The generated source is not committed — this tarball ships it under `src/`, and the provenance attestation names the exact commit it came from, so you can regenerate and compare.

To report a problem or request a change to the API surface, open an issue in [formbricks/hub](https://github.com/formbricks/hub/issues).

# Formbricks Hub documentation

The documentation site for [hub.formbricks.com](https://hub.formbricks.com), built with
[Astro](https://astro.build) and [Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build).

The API reference is generated from `../openapi.yaml` — the same spec the Go server is
built against — by [`starlight-openapi`](https://starlight-openapi.vercel.app/). There is
no external service in the build: `pnpm build` works offline with no API keys.

## Commands

Run these from this directory (`docs/`):

| Command        | What it does                                         |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm install` | Install dependencies                                 |
| `pnpm dev`     | Dev server at http://localhost:4321                  |
| `pnpm build`   | Production build into `dist/`                        |
| `pnpm preview` | Serve the built site locally                         |
| `pnpm check`   | `astro check` — types and content-collection schemas |
| `pnpm format`  | Prettier across this directory                       |

## Layout

- `src/content/docs/` — the pages (`.md`/`.mdx`). Landing page is `index.mdx`.
- `src/content/docs/core-concepts/`, `guides/`, `reference/` — the three prose sections.
- `astro.config.ts` — site config, sidebar topics, and the OpenAPI reference wiring.
- `src/assets/` — images imported from content.
- `public/` — served as-is (favicons, web manifest).
- `theme.css` — brand overrides on top of Starlight's defaults.

## Editing

Prose pages are Markdown/MDX with Starlight frontmatter (`title`, `description`). Use
Starlight's [components](https://starlight.astro.build/components/using-components/) —
`<Aside>`, `<Card>`, `<LinkButton>`, `<Tabs>` — imported from
`@astrojs/starlight/components`.

The API reference is not hand-written. To change it, change `../openapi.yaml`.

package tests

import (
	"context"
	"testing"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

	"github.com/formbricks/hub/internal/config"
	"github.com/formbricks/hub/internal/models"
	"github.com/formbricks/hub/internal/repository"
	"github.com/formbricks/hub/pkg/database"
)

const searchTestModel = "search-test-model"

// searchVec builds a deterministic unit-ish vector whose cosine distance to searchVec(0) grows
// with n, so ordering assertions are exact: dimension 0 carries the signal, dimension 1 the rest.
func searchVec(n float64) []float32 {
	vec := make([]float32, models.EmbeddingVectorDimensions)
	vec[0] = float32(1 - n/10)
	vec[1] = float32(n / 10)

	return vec
}

// TestSemanticSearch_NearestFeedbackRecords executes the real nearest-neighbor SQL end to end —
// the one read path every layer above mocks (the COALESCE regression shipped through four review
// passes precisely because nothing ran these queries): ordering, tenant isolation, excludeID,
// minScore filtering, NULL-field-label coalescing, and keyset continuation via the cursor variant.
func TestSemanticSearch_NearestFeedbackRecords(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()

	cfg, err := config.Load()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	db, err := database.NewPostgresPool(ctx, cfg.Database.URL, database.WithPoolConfig(cfg.Database.PoolConfig()))
	require.NoError(t, err)

	defer db.Close()

	recordsRepo := repository.NewFeedbackRecordsRepository(db)
	embeddingsRepo := repository.NewEmbeddingsRepository(db)

	tenantA := testTenantID("search-a")
	tenantB := testTenantID("search-b")

	mkEmbedded := func(tenantID, text string, label *string, closeness float64) uuid.UUID {
		valueText := text
		rec, createErr := recordsRepo.Create(ctx, &models.CreateFeedbackRecordRequest{
			SourceType:   "formbricks",
			FieldID:      "q1",
			FieldLabel:   label,
			FieldType:    models.FieldTypeText,
			ValueText:    &valueText,
			TenantID:     tenantID,
			SubmissionID: testTenantID("sub"),
		})
		require.NoError(t, createErr)
		require.NoError(t, embeddingsRepo.Upsert(ctx, rec.ID, searchTestModel, searchVec(closeness), nil))

		return rec.ID
	}

	label := "How was it?"
	nearest := mkEmbedded(tenantA, "closest text", &label, 0)
	middle := mkEmbedded(tenantA, "middle text", nil, 2) // NULL field_label -> COALESCE to ""
	far := mkEmbedded(tenantA, "far text", &label, 5)
	otherTenant := mkEmbedded(tenantB, "other tenant text", &label, 0)

	query := searchVec(0)

	t.Run("orders by distance, isolates tenants, fills labels", func(t *testing.T) {
		results, _, searchErr := embeddingsRepo.NearestFeedbackRecordsByEmbedding(
			ctx, searchTestModel, query, tenantA, 10, nil, 0)
		require.NoError(t, searchErr)
		require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(results), 3)

		assert.Equal(t, nearest, results[0].FeedbackRecordID, "closest vector first")
		assert.Equal(t, "How was it?", results[0].FieldLabel)
		assert.Equal(t, middle, results[1].FeedbackRecordID)
		assert.Empty(t, results[1].FieldLabel, "NULL field_label coalesces to empty")
		assert.Equal(t, far, results[2].FeedbackRecordID)
		assert.NotEmpty(t, results[0].ValueText, "value_text is projected")

		for _, r := range results {
			assert.NotEqual(t, otherTenant, r.FeedbackRecordID, "tenant B rows never leak into tenant A search")
			assert.InDelta(t, 1-r.Distance, r.Score, 1e-9, "score is 1 - distance")
		}
	})

	t.Run("excludeID drops the anchor record", func(t *testing.T) {
		results, _, searchErr := embeddingsRepo.NearestFeedbackRecordsByEmbedding(
			ctx, searchTestModel, query, tenantA, 10, &nearest, 0)
		require.NoError(t, searchErr)

		for _, r := range results {
			assert.NotEqual(t, nearest, r.FeedbackRecordID)
		}
	})

	t.Run("minScore filters far rows", func(t *testing.T) {
		results, _, searchErr := embeddingsRepo.NearestFeedbackRecordsByEmbedding(
			ctx, searchTestModel, query, tenantA, 10, nil, 0.99)
		require.NoError(t, searchErr)

		ids := make(map[uuid.UUID]bool, len(results))
		for _, r := range results {
			ids[r.FeedbackRecordID] = true
			assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, r.Score, 0.99)
		}

		assert.True(t, ids[nearest], "the identical vector passes the threshold")
		assert.False(t, ids[far], "the far vector is filtered out")
	})

	t.Run("cursor page is a disjoint continuation", func(t *testing.T) {
		page1, hasMore, searchErr := embeddingsRepo.NearestFeedbackRecordsByEmbedding(
			ctx, searchTestModel, query, tenantA, 1, nil, 0)
		require.NoError(t, searchErr)
		require.Len(t, page1, 1)
		assert.True(t, hasMore, "more rows exist past a 1-row page")

		last := page1[0]
		page2, _, searchErr := embeddingsRepo.NearestFeedbackRecordsByEmbeddingAfterCursor(
			ctx, searchTestModel, query, tenantA, 10, last.Distance, last.FeedbackRecordID, nil, 0)
		require.NoError(t, searchErr)
		require.NotEmpty(t, page2)

		for _, r := range page2 {
			assert.NotEqual(t, last.FeedbackRecordID, r.FeedbackRecordID, "page 2 never repeats the cursor row")
			assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, r.Distance, last.Distance, "page 2 continues at or past the cursor distance")
		}

		assert.Equal(t, middle, page2[0].FeedbackRecordID, "page 2 starts at the next-nearest row")
	})
}
